statements.t: Consolidating our tobacco processing operations in Brazil will create operating efficiencies through the centralization of processing and receiving activities, which we expect to improve factory utilization and provide long-term cost structure improvements.
A portion of the proceeds from this sale will be used to invest in continued automation capabilities and other efficiency upgrades at our Venâncio Aires facility.
The current El Niño cycle continues to unfold and is expected to reach its peak effects between the Company's third and fourth quarters of fiscal 2027.
During such time, our liquidity needs for operations may approach the levels of our anticipated available cash and permitted borrowings under our credit facilities.
To address a potential liquidity deficiency, we may undertake plans to minimize cash outflows, which could include exiting operations that do not generate positive cash flow.

A limitation associated with using net debt is that it subtracts cash and cash equivalents, and therefore, may imply that management intends to use cash and cash equivalents to reduce outstanding debt and that cash held in certain jurisdictions can be applied to repay obligations owing in other jurisdictions and without reduction for applicable taxes.
We will continue to monitor and hedge foreign currency costs, as needed.
Capital spend for fiscal year 2027 includes strategic projects to drive long-term efficiencies and cost optimization at our largest operations in Africa and South America.

For the six months ended September 30, 2026, we incurred approximately $11.8 million in capital expenditures, and are expecting to incur an additional $26.1 million for the remainder of the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027.

estimates.t: There have been no material changes to our critical accounting estimates since March 31, 2026.

statements.t: "Our improved margins and strong ongoing customer demand further support our outlook, and we are tightening our full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance."

The Company is adjusting its fiscal year 2027 outlook by narrowing its guidance range for Adjusted EBITDA to reflect improved visibility into expected operating performance for the second half of the fiscal year.

Based on results through the second quarter and current business trends, the Company continues to expect fiscal year 2027 net sales of $2.3 billion to $2.5 billion, and Adjusted EBITDA is now expected to be between $215 million and $235 million, compared to the prior guidance range of $210 million to $240 million.
This release, as well as the Company’s second quarter results presentation, will be available on the Company's investor relations webpage prior to the call.
For those unable to join the live audio webcast, an archived recording will be available on the Company's investor relations webpage shortly after the call.
